study: Carroll et al. (2020), Bug Club whole-school reading programme (Pearson) RCT, The Curriculum Journal
eval_evidence: Independent academic evaluators (Carroll, Hurry et al., UCL/St Mary's University) conducted an RCT of Pearson's commercial Bug Club programme; the evaluators are not the developer (Pearson).
developer_evidence: Teachers were trained for implementation shortly before rollout, but the publication does not state the developers/research team delivered the PD; Bug Club is a commercial Pearson product and the evaluators are independent. Training appears to be vendor/implementation training, not researcher-delivered.
cascade_evidence: 'Teachers received training in the implementation of Bug Club ... shortly before implementation', but the report does not identify who delivered the training or any train-the-trainer tier, so transmission depth cannot be determined.
counterfactual_evidence: Waiting-list control on the standard national KS1 English/Literacy programmes of study (business-as-usual); control adopted Bug Club only in Year 2 (after the A1 primary contrast).
coaching_evidence: Teachers received implementation training shortly before rollout; no ongoing in-class coaching of teachers is described in the report.
student_dose_evidence: Beyond teacher instruction, pupils get a substantial student-facing digital dose: online Bug Club books assigned to each child's account for independent/at-home reading with embedded comprehension/phonics questions reported back to the teacher (plus print home-reading books).
maturity_evidence: A1 primary outcome (July 2015) is measured after two terms of the schools' first implementation of Bug Club, with teachers new to the programme.
